newsitem.title: UK: Focus shifts to dollars in quiet Eurobond session.
newsitem.headline: Focus shifts to dollars in quiet Eurobond session.

text.p: The sell-off in U.S. Treasuries on Friday following strong U.S. payrolls data, together with wider swap spreads, allowed borrowers to achieve tighter funding with a higher coupon, bankers said on Monday.
GECC quickly took advantage with a $300 million seven-year bond, which paid a 6.25 percent coupon and offered 17 basis points over five-year U.S. Treasury notes, or around 13 b.p. over the curve.
"We have had a surprisingly strong response to the deal, considering it is August and a Monday morning," a syndicate manager at joint lead Paribas said.
"We have already sold around 40 percent of our ticket."
He said there was institutional and retail buying, with interest sparked by the yield pick-up in seven-year dollar paper relative to five-year bonds.
"GECC at five years would only offer a spread in the mid single digits," the Paribas official said. ABN AMRO Hoare Govett was the other joint lead manager.

On the foreign exchanges, the dollar/mark rate was expected to set a new 7.5-year high if reports this week show German economic growth is not strong enough to allow higher interest rates. The dollar's strength was also underpinning demand for dollar debt.
On the emerging market side, Banco de Galicia y Buenos Aires launched a $100 million five-year bond, to be priced at 165-170 b.p. over Treasuries.
Later today Rabobank Brazil was expected to issue a $100 million three-year bond via ABN AMRO and Bear Stearns, bankers said.
Later this week, Sanwa Business Credit Corp will launch a $200 million five-year FRN. Merrill Lynch International and Sanwa international will likely lead manage the deal.
U.S.-based finance company Sanwa Business Credit Corp, rated Aa3 by Moodys and A- by S&P, is owned by Sanwa Bank Ltd. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
